reports.title: SINAPROC #31: 22,245 homes evaluated, 4,503 with total damage; 91 shelters
reports.summary: COE Nacional (13 Nov): 22,245 homes evaluated covering 70,306 people; 4,503 with total damage, 10,836 moderate or partial, 4,504 minor. 91 shelters remain active, mostly in Veraguas and Los Santos; IMA has delivered 82,530 food bags; 40 of 46 heritage sites evaluated, 19 being shored up.

reports.title: UN Situation Report 9: 2,731 in shelters; WFP cash aid from early December
reports.summary: UN/OCHA (11 Nov): 2,731 people in 100 shelters, a fifth fewer than a week earlier; MIDES has surveyed 8,000+ households (24,000+ people) to target aid, and WFP plans cash assistance from early December. Temporary learning spaces could serve ~5,500 students; sanitation at the temporary Los Pozos hospital is critically deficient.
reports.source_name: UN Country Team / OCHA via ReliefWeb

reports.title: MIVIOT: 75 contracts for 4,197 replacement homes in five provinces
reports.summary: Panamá Compra records reviewed by La Prensa: 75 emergency contracts worth US$124.08M with 21 firms to build 4,197 homes in Los Santos, Veraguas, Herrera, Coclé and Chiriquí, at about US$28,000–30,000 per home, funded from the US$100M emergency trust at Banco Nacional.

reports.title: Cabinet sets three housing options: new home, cash equivalent or repair grant
reports.summary: Cabinet Resolution No. 34 (Gaceta Oficial 13 Nov): families with destroyed or damaged homes can get a new MIVIOT home on the same plot regardless of land title, cash equal to the value of that home, or a cash grant for repair materials and labour. Caja de Ahorros and Banco Nacional are told to advance working capital to contractors.

reports.title: MIVIOT: 38,000 damage reports received; 4,000–6,000 homes need rebuilding
reports.summary: Housing minister Jaime Jované: the MIVIOT platform has received 38,000+ reports of damaged homes and 16,000+ have been evaluated; between 4,000 and 6,000 have total damage and must be rebuilt, while repairs go through a separate programme.

reports.title: Secretariat of Goals: 4,000+ homes in contracting; repair evaluations move to Isla Cañas and Macaracas
reports.summary: José Ramón Icaza (Secretaría de Metas): more than 4,000 new homes are in the contracting process; repair evaluations started in Tonosí, are now in Isla Cañas and move to Macaracas, then other districts. The Government is seeking more contractors and SPIA engineers, and wants local labour hired.

reports.title: Health minister: rebuilding damaged hospitals will cost about US$160M
reports.summary: Health minister Fernando Boyd Galindo said reconstruction of seriously damaged health facilities will cost about US$160M, and listed facilities already back in service in the most affected provinces.

reports.title: CSS: Remón, San Cristóbal, Los Pozos and Tonosí units still closed or in temporary sites
reports.summary: CSS (15 Nov): Policlínica Presidente Remón and ULAPS San Cristóbal remain closed; CAPPS Los Pozos works from the municipal court and ULAPS Tonosí from a tent hospital. Chitré's Roberto Ramírez polyclinic runs from a modular unit; Soná and Santiago hospitals operate with closed areas; boiler repairs at Chitré's Nelson Collado hospital start 16 Nov.

reports.place: San Miguelito and Plaza 5 de Mayo, Panama City
reports.title: CSS closes two senior wellbeing centres in Panama City over quake damage
reports.summary: The CSS suspended its Centros de Bienestar in San Miguelito and Plaza 5 de Mayo (13 Nov) because of structural damage from the 9 Oct earthquake; users are redirected to Parque Lefevre. No reopening date given.

reports.title: IDAAN: 26 of 45 water tanks inspected have critical damage
reports.summary: IDAAN told the Cabinet that 26 of 45 storage tanks reviewed have critical damage; 19 tanker trucks have delivered 100,000 gallons. Worst case: the 400,000-gallon tank at the Roberto Reyna plant in Chitré is out of service, limiting pressure in parts of the city; the Santa Marta (Bugaba) plant was also damaged.

reports.title: Photo: collapsed water tank leaves 300+ in Farfán without supply
reports.summary: The earthquake toppled the water storage tank serving Farfán, Soná district, leaving more than 300 residents without piped water; CONADES will install a new tank. MINSA is also evaluating a permanent fix for other aqueducts that collapsed in Soná.

reports.title: MOP to take plan to repair 16–17 quake-damaged bridges to Cabinet
reports.summary: Public works minister José Luis Andrade: landslide debris has been almost fully removed and all roads are open; a proposal to repair 16–17 damaged bridges goes to the Cabinet soon. Slope stabilisation is still being assessed (including in Herrera), heavy equipment remains at Búcaro, and the Macaracas–Tonosí road will be tendered.

reports.title: Fire service: four stations damaged; David central and Gualaca stations to be demolished
reports.summary: Fire chief Víctor Álvarez said at least four fire stations were damaged by the earthquakes; the Juan N. Araúz central station in David and the Gualaca station must be demolished, and the others are still being evaluated.

reports.title: Pesé public library declared unfit for use
reports.summary: SINAPROC and municipal engineers declared the José Daniel Crespo public library in Pesé (Herrera) unfit for occupation because of structural damage; the Ministry of Culture closed it temporarily.

reports.title: School year 2027 to start 1 March despite damaged schools
reports.summary: Education minister Ventura Vega said classes start on 1 March 2027 as planned; some damaged schools will be demolished and rebuilt, and MEDUCA is preparing alternative spaces so that no student is left without classes.

reports.title: UNICEF and EU run child-friendly spaces for 6,800+ children
reports.summary: UNICEF, with European Union funding, is providing child-friendly spaces with psychosocial and learning support to more than 6,800 children affected by the earthquake (EFE, Macaracas, 16 Nov).

reports.title: Geociencias: 1,500+ aftershocks, now ~20 a day; may continue 2–3 months
reports.summary: Néstor Luque (Instituto de Geociencias, UP): more than 1,500 aftershocks since 9 Oct, down from 60–70 a day in the first weeks to about 20 a day of M3–4; larger events remain possible and activity may continue for two to three months.

reports.title: M4.8 aftershock 29 km south of Soná, felt in Panama City
reports.summary: Instituto de Geociencias reported a preliminary M4.8 at 13:57 local on 12 Nov, 29 km south of Soná at ~5 km depth; it followed an M4.8 near Tonosí on 11 Nov that was felt in the capital. No new damage reported.

reports.title: MICI opens online form for businesses damaged by the quake
reports.summary: The Ministry of Commerce and Industries opened a digital form for shops and industries in Coclé, Veraguas, Herrera and Los Santos to report damage and needs; 73 firms had earlier reported losses.

reports.title: Banks ready to offer payment arrangements to affected clients
reports.summary: The Asociación Bancaria de Panamá says member banks will consider payment arrangements and other relief for clients hit by the earthquake; most damaged homes were not bank-financed, but owners may have other loans.

reports.title: Pedasí waives municipal taxes for 12 months on quake repairs
reports.summary: Pedasí's municipal council approved a 100% exemption from municipal taxes on repair, reinforcement and rebuilding of homes, hotels and shops damaged by the earthquake (Acuerdo 21, Gaceta Oficial 12 Nov), subject to a municipal engineer's evaluation.

reports.title: Santa Catalina: coastline changes hit fishing, surfing and tourism
reports.summary: Panamá América reports that the earthquake reshaped the coast at Santa Catalina (Soná), hurting artisanal fishing, surf tourism and the local economy; hostels in southern Veraguas (Mariato) report empty rooms and rising unemployment.

reports.title: University of Panama economists: regional losses could reach US$2bn
reports.summary: Reyes Valverde (CIFE, Universidad de Panamá) estimates losses of up to US$2,000M in Coclé, Veraguas, Herrera and Los Santos (7.7% of GDP combined), from homes, roads, farm roads and livestock and poultry damage. Academic model, not an official assessment.
